d2_fold_in.requirement: Develop and implement a monitoring plan kept on file for State and public review, complete no later than the initial Subpart V monitoring date, containing monitoring locations, monitoring dates, compliance calculation procedures, and plans for other systems in the combined distribution system where the State reduced requirements under 142.16(m)

Systems without an IDSE report and with too few subpart L locations identify additional compliance monitoring locations by alternating selection of high-TTHM and high-HAA5 locations, with rationale; systems with more subpart L locations than needed choose by the same alternation
Subpart H systems serving more than 3,300 people submit a copy of the monitoring plan to the State before initial monitoring unless the IDSE report already contains the required information

Plan revisions for treatment, distribution or layout changes after State consultation; changed locations replace the lowest-LRAA locations with expected high TTHM or HAA5 locations; the State may require modifications; subpart H systems over 3,300 submit the modified plan before complying with it

Remaining on reduced monitoring after the 141.620(c) dates requires a 40/30 certification under 141.603 or a very small system waiver under 141.604, plus the 141.623(a) criteria, with no change or addition of monitoring locations from subpart L
If Subpart V monitoring locations differ from subpart L locations, the system may not remain on reduced monitoring after the 141.620(c) dates

A system on increased monitoring under 141.132(b)(1) remains on increased monitoring under 141.625 at the 141.622 plan locations from the 141.620(c) date until it qualifies for a return to routine monitoring under 141.625(c)

Subpart L applies to CWSs and NTNCWSs that add a chemical disinfectant in any part of treatment: they must meet the MCLs in 141.64, the MRDLs in 141.65 and the precursor treatment technique in 141.135
Transient NCWSs that use chlorine dioxide as a disinfectant or oxidant must meet the chlorine dioxide MRDL in 141.65
Informational statement of purpose naming the regulated byproducts; not a requirement. Compositions are already claims on dbp.definitions

Compliance dates for CWSs and NTNCWSs: subpart H systems serving 10,000 or more from January 1, 2002; subpart H systems under 10,000 and ground water systems not under the direct influence of surface water from January 1, 2004
Compliance dates for transient NCWSs using chlorine dioxide: the same two dates by the same size and source split
Each regulated CWS and NTNCWS must be operated by qualified personnel meeting State requirements and listed in the State register of qualified operators

Notwithstanding the MRDLs, systems may raise chlorine or chloramine residuals (not chlorine dioxide) to the level and for the time needed to protect public health during specified microbiological contamination events
